h1: Triple B Sleep and Relax Korat — a Stylish Budget Stay in Central Nakhon Ratchasima
intro: If you're after a place to stay in Korat that's light on the wallet but still looks good, Triple B Sleep and Relax is a name guests bring up again and again · A small 19-room boutique hotel decorated in a brick-walled loft style, it opened in 2017 and was freshly renovated in 2024, and sits on Suranarai Road in central Nakhon Ratchasima, about 1 kilometre from Central Korat · What guests praise over and over is the soft beds and pillows, clean rooms that look new, and friendly staff · There's free coffee and Ovaltine and drinking water, free Wi-Fi, and free parking · From about THB 690/night, with a review score as high as 8.9

body.html: Triple B Sleep and Relax is a small boutique hotel that plenty of people on social media casually call Korat's "stylish stay for a few hundred baht" · The hotel has been open since 2017 and only recently went through a major renovation in 2024, so the furniture, walls and interiors all feel fresh and new · Its positioning is fairly clear: it's a place for people who want a good-looking, well-designed room on a budget that won't hurt, rather than a big hotel packed with every amenity · With just 19 rooms, the overall feel is quieter and more private than a large hotel, with no tour groups milling about — a good fit for couples, solo travellers, small families, or anyone driving through Korat who just wants a clean place to rest their head in town without paying a lot · The name "Triple B" and the words Sleep and Relax capture the concept well: it's about sleeping comfortably and unwinding without overthinking it, which shows up in the reviews that mostly talk about the beds and the peace and quiet.

Location is the main advantage here · Triple B sits on Suranarai Road Soi 15 in Ban Ko subdistrict, a central area of Nakhon Ratchasima, with access from both Suranarai Road and Mittraphap Road, so getting into town or heading off elsewhere is easy · From the hotel it's just a few minutes' drive to Central Plaza Nakhon Ratchasima (about 1 kilometre), which is very close for anyone who wants to wander the mall, catch a film, or grab food at the shopping centre in the evening · Terminal 21 Korat, another popular mall, is about 5 kilometres away · Around the hotel there are also plenty of food spots and markets to stroll through — Ban Ko Market with its local eats, RN Yard (a relaxed young-crowd food-and-drink yard), and the nearby Solar Market · Close by are Nakhon Ratchasima Rajabhat University and Rajamangala University of Technology Isan, which means the neighbourhood is dotted with restaurants, coffee shops and chill hangouts popular with the younger crowd · For visitors into spiritual or cultural sights, the Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo), a landmark of Korat, and Wat Sala Loi are a short drive from the city centre.

When it comes to getting around, if you arrive by car it's fairly convenient because there's free parking and the location has multiple routes in and out of town · Korat is a city many people stop in on the way up to Khao Yai or onward to the upper Isan region, so having on-site parking is an advantage that saves you circling around looking for a spot outside · For those arriving by coach or van, the Nakhon Ratchasima bus terminal and the train station are within a not-too-far drive (the train station is about 7 kilometres away), but the hotel's soi may need a quick Grab or motorbike taxi to reach, since it isn't right on a main road where you can walk to a bus stop straight away · This is normal for a boutique stay tucked in a soi, the trade-off being quiet and a lack of crowds · Past guests consistently suggest that driving yourself is the most convenient option, since you get both parking and the ease of heading out to eat and explore around the city — especially for dinner, when you might want to try several places.

There are 19 rooms in total, decorated in a brick-walled loft style (Cozy Loft) in warm tones, mixing bare concrete with wooden furniture and looking more designed than the price suggests · There are several types to choose from, from a Twin room with two 3.5-foot single beds, to Double / Double-King rooms with a 6-foot bed, up to a Super King room with an extra-large 7-foot bed, and a Family Suite with two bedrooms, a living area and a separate balcony for families or small groups · What guests mention most is that the beds and pillows really are soft and comfy, with many reviews saying something like "the bed is super comfortable, the pillows are so soft", which fits the hotel's Sleep and Relax concept · The bathrooms are done in black-and-white tones, looking clean and modern with new fixtures, and reviews praise the shower's good water pressure, so showering is comfortable with no guesswork · Rooms come with coffee, Ovaltine, an electric kettle and free drinking water, plus plenty of power outlets to charge your devices easily — handy for anyone travelling with a lot of gadgets.
"Beautiful, clean room, super comfortable bed and really soft pillows. The staff were lovely and well-spoken. If you come to Korat you have to stay here — great value at this price."

On the amenities front, Triple B positions itself as a small boutique stay that focuses on getting the basics right and clean rather than offering a pool or gym like a big hotel · There's free Wi-Fi in all rooms, a 24-hour front desk, a small in-house convenience store/mini-mart, and key-card security with staff on hand · There's room service, luggage storage, and a washing machine for longer stays, which is very handy for anyone travelling several days or on a long trip · What guests are repeatedly impressed by is the friendly, helpful staff — many reviews mention their politeness and the small touches that make it feel as warm as staying at a friend's place · As for food, even though there's a small shop area and seating corner on site, the real strength is the location, surrounded by restaurants and markets in town, making it easy to find a bite for both breakfast and dinner without relying on the hotel · Many guests head out for Korat pad mee, freshly stir-fried Korat noodles, or local eats at the markets near the hotel instead.
"Brand-new, clean room, not expensive, nicely decorated and photogenic, easy parking, lovely staff. The only shame is there's no lift — for the upper floors you have to carry your bags up yourself."

The thing to know before booking, and the most common complaint from reading through reviews, is that the building is a 3-storey block with no lift · If you get an upper-floor room you'll have to lug your bags up the stairs yourself, which many reviews agree isn't very convenient for the elderly, anyone with a lot of luggage, or people who find stairs difficult · If you're in that group, it's best to tell the hotel at the time of booking that you'd like a ground-floor room, which the hotel can usually arrange if one is free · There are also occasional reviews about the air-con being a bit noisy in some rooms, and a post mentioning an extra charge for a third guest (about 300 baht) with no special add-on services included, so it's worth checking the terms clearly before booking if you're coming as a group · Another thing to understand is that this is a small place, so there's no pool, gym, or breakfast buffet like a big hotel · Overall these notes are manageable by choosing your room and asking ahead, and they're not big enough issues to drag the review score down.

To be straight with you, from reading real reviews across Agoda, Booking and Wongnai, the overall picture of Triple B Sleep and Relax leans clearly positive · It's better suited to people who want a good-looking, stylish stay on a few-hundred-baht budget in central Korat than to those after a big hotel with a pool and a full set of amenities · The strengths guests agree on are cleanliness, soft beds, photogenic decor that punches above its price, and good service · The main limitations come back to the lack of a lift and the soi location, which may mean relying on a car if you don't have transport · With a review score as high as around 8.9 from a large number of guests, and repeated praise about "good value" and "you have to stay here when you come to Korat", it's safe to say this is one of the budget stays in Korat that guests are most happy with.

The food around the hotel is another thing that makes Triple B's location appealing · Korat is known for Isan food and local dishes like Korat pad mee with its chewy noodles, punchy som tam, and roadside grills, which aren't hard to find in this neighbourhood · Ban Ko Market near the hotel has food from early evening into the night, perfect for anyone who wants to head out for a casual bite after check-in, while RN Yard is a relaxed young-crowd drinking yard with rotating vendors and an easy-going vibe · If you want a café to sip morning coffee before heading out, the area around the universities has several nice coffee shops a short drive away · For those who prefer air-conditioned mall strolling, Central Korat, just about 1 kilometre away, has chain restaurants, a food court and a cinema · So even though the hotel itself doesn't focus on in-house food, the location makes up for it, and guests don't have to worry about finding a meal, with options all around from street food to mall restaurants.

Comparing value with other stays in Korat at a similar price, Triple B comes out ahead on design and freshness · In the roughly 700–800 baht range, many places in town still offer old-hotel-style or plain guesthouse rooms, while Triple B gives you freshly decorated loft-style rooms, soft beds, and extras like free coffee and Ovaltine, which makes it feel like you're getting more than you pay for · Compared with budget chain hotels in town like the B2 group or other central boutique hotels, Triple B wins on the quiet, private atmosphere and the decor, but loses on the lift and the number of amenities · In short, if you weight "a beautiful, clean room that's comfortable to sleep in at a budget price" over "full amenities and a lift", this is a worthwhile pick to book in Korat.

Tips from reading the reviews: if you're coming with elderly travellers or have a lot of luggage, ask for a ground-floor room when you book, since the building has no lift · If you want a bigger room with an extra-large bed, choose the Super King or Family Suite, which have a seating area and balcony · If you're driving, make the most of the free parking and plan to head out for dinner at the in-town markets nearby, such as Ban Ko Market, or stroll the mall at Central Korat just about 1 kilometre away · If you're coming as a group, don't forget to check the terms on the third-guest charge before booking so there are no surprise costs at check-in · And as always, room rates shift with festival periods and long weekends, especially when people stop over before heading up to Khao Yai, so it's worth comparing prices across several platforms — Agoda, Booking and Trip.com — every time before you book to get the best deal.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Triple B Sleep and Relax Korat

faq.q: Where is Triple B Sleep and Relax Korat, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's at 14/4 Suranarai Road Soi 15, Ban Ko subdistrict, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima district, in central Korat, with access from both Suranarai Road and Mittraphap · It's about 1 kilometre from Central Plaza Nakhon Ratchasima and about 5 kilometres from Terminal 21 Korat · There's free parking, ideal for those driving themselves, while those without a car may need a Grab or motorbike taxi to get in and out of the soi.

faq.q: How much does Triple B Sleep and Relax start at, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 690/night for a Twin or Double Bed room · The Super King room with an extra-large bed starts at about THB 790, and the Family Suite with 2 bedrooms plus a living area and balcony starts at about THB 1,290 · Rates shift with festival periods and long weekends, so it's best to compare several platforms before booking each time.

faq.q: What are the rooms at Triple B Sleep and Relax like, and are they clean?
faq.a: The rooms are decorated in a brick-walled loft style in warm tones and were freshly renovated in 2024, so they look new and designed · Guests praise the cleanliness, the soft, comfy beds and pillows, and the modern-looking black-and-white bathroom with good water pressure · Rooms come with coffee, Ovaltine, a kettle and free drinking water, plus plenty of power outlets — great for anyone wanting a beautiful room at a budget price.

faq.q: Does Triple B Sleep and Relax have a lift, and is it suitable for the elderly?
faq.a: The building is a 3-storey block with no lift, so if you get an upper-floor room you'll have to carry your bags up the stairs yourself, which many reviews say isn't very convenient for the elderly or anyone with a lot of luggage · If you're in that group, it's best to ask the hotel for a ground-floor room at the time of booking.

faq.q: What parking and amenities does Triple B Sleep and Relax have?
faq.a: There's free parking, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk, a small in-house convenience store/mini-mart, and key-card security with staff on hand · There's room service, luggage storage, and a washing machine for longer stays · What guests like is the free coffee, Ovaltine and drinking water in the room, along with the friendly, well-spoken staff.

faq.q: Who is Triple B Sleep and Relax good for?
faq.a: It's good for couples, solo travellers, small families, or anyone driving through Korat who wants a beautiful, stylish stay on a few-hundred-baht budget · If you want a clean room, soft bed and design that punches above its price, in a central location near malls and markets, and you're not fussed about there being no lift or luxury amenities — this offers value that's among the most popular with guests in Korat.
